newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 1.607 billion yuan from 1.478 billion yuan last Friday with the 60-day contract the most active.
Traders said that active trading in the A share market supported the rates despite the central bank setting a lower interest rate subsidy.
The People's Bank of China, the central bank, announced at the weekend an interest rate subsidy of 0.17 percent for April, down from the March subsidy of 0.94 percent.
"Continuous falls in the interest rate subsidy show that China's inflation is being successfully controlled, which will prevent the rates from rising in the mid-term," a trader said.

But recent rises on the domestic A share market were supporting the rates with speculators encouraged to buy on the interbank market, while major state banks continued to be major sellers, traders said.
On Monday, Shanghai's A share index jumped 2.96 percent to end at a year high of 1,212.753 points on volume of 1.1 billion shares worth 12 billion yuan, the heaviest trade in 1997.
"The rates will move up if the A share market continues to rise in the next few days," a second trader said.
Several new A share listings and issues also contributed to the day's active trading, traders said.
